reason: Add a mature-OSS-first local auxiliary AI layer without changing Yance's authoritative real-time chat quality. The real-time reply path remains cloud Model Brain/LiteLLM only; local models are optional, asynchronous, independently scheduled helpers for background understanding, summarization, extraction and relationship intelligence. V1 extends the already-present Ollama integration instead of inventing a Yance inference engine, adds on-demand model asset management and capability/SLA evidence, and makes local runtime failure, slowness, missing models or missing Ollama zero-effect on formal real-time reply availability and latency. Low-resource machines may use quantized/larger local models only in background roles proven by benchmark/qualification; no local model is silently promoted into real-time reply authority.

digestCanonicalization.pathNormalization: Require exact repository-relative normalized paths, remove duplicates, then sort with JavaScript default Array.prototype.sort().
digestCanonicalization.canonicalText: Join the normalized sorted unique path list with LF and append exactly one trailing LF before hashing.

expectedFailures: A verified local Ollama deployment is currently eligible for formal reply logical groups when its task tags match; the new product contract requires formal quick/deep/director reply candidates to be cloud-only.
Current background AI jobs and formal reply jobs share the AiGateway Model Brain queue, so a slow local background execution can consume concurrency needed by interactive cloud work.
Ollama discovery exists but V1 has no governed on-demand pull/progress/cancel lifecycle for approved local model assets.
Current status surfaces do not distinguish local auxiliary capability/benchmark/SLA evidence from real-time reply authority.

The trusted implementationBranchPolicy parser recognizes the exact implementation path set, failure-first path set and Fast Closure V2 diagnostic-window semantics.

The current Product UAT exact-head branch/artifacts remain untouched; this P1 branch starts from trusted main and does not rewrite/reuse the UAT candidate lineage.

local model qualification, allowedTasks and lifecycle projection
AI Workbench/System Center user controls and truthful degraded/unavailable states

localAuxiliary.largeLowResourceModelRule: A large/quantized local model may be admitted only to background tasks whose measured SLA it satisfies; runnable does not imply real-time eligible.

forbiddenBehavior: Do not replace formal cloud reply with a local model because local hardware or a local model is available.
Do not make a formal reply wait for local inference, local model download, local benchmark or local runtime startup.
Do not silently downgrade reply quality to a smaller local model.
Do not implement a second physical model router or duplicate LiteLLM retry/fallback/provider-selection authority.
Do not add KTransformers, AirLLM, llama.cpp or another runtime in V1 without fresh OSS-fit evidence and a merged same-work-package scope amendment.
Do not weaken Model Brain qualification, durable AI execution authority, stale-generation fencing or current reply evidence contracts.

reviewedCandidates.name: Ollama
reviewedCandidates.reason: Yance already discovers, streams, unloads and deletes Ollama models. V1 extends this mature runtime seam with governed pull/progress/cancel and auxiliary-only scheduling instead of adding a new inference engine.

reviewedCandidates.name: LiteLLM
reviewedCandidates.reason: Already owns formal cloud model physical routing, retries, fallback, cooldown and health; V1 must preserve this authority for real-time replies.

reviewedCandidates.name: llama.cpp
reviewedCandidates.reason: Mature and valuable for low-resource GGUF execution, but V1 does not add a second runtime until packaged Windows provenance, lifecycle isolation and measurable benefit over the existing Ollama seam are proven in a separate exact-scope admission.

reviewedCandidates.name: KTransformers / AirLLM
reviewedCandidates.reason: Do not place experimental or higher-operational-risk large-model runtimes on the formal product path before Windows maturity, reproducibility and crash-isolation evidence exists.

retireOrAvoid: Do not create a second Yance physical model router, provider scorer, retry/fallback authority or inference engine; preserve LiteLLM for formal cloud routing and extend the existing Ollama seam for local auxiliary execution.
Do not duplicate Ollama discovery, stream execution, unload or delete paths; extend backend/services/ollamaClient.js and the existing Model Brain projections instead.
Do not add KTransformers, AirLLM, llama.cpp or another local runtime in V1, and do not create any local prerequisite or fallback path for quick_reply, deep_reply or director.

negativeProofs: With no Ollama service, formal cloud reply candidate projection and execution remain available.
With an intentionally hung/failing local auxiliary task, interactive cloud queue capacity and formal reply latency contract remain unaffected.
A qualified local model cannot become a quick_reply/deep_reply/director deployment.
Model download, benchmark and lifecycle operations are never prerequisites for formal reply.
No second physical routing/scoring authority appears outside LiteLLM.
